evals.name: ml-startup-pitch
evals.prompt: Create a pitch deck for my ML startup called 'DataForge'. Include a user growth chart showing 1K, 5K, 20K, 80K users over Q1-Q4, a bar chart comparing our model accuracy (94%) vs competitors (87%, 82%), and an architecture diagram showing our microservices setup with API Gateway, Model Service, Data Pipeline, and PostgreSQL.
evals.expected_output: A 10 or more slide DataForge pitch deck that uses the supplied growth and accuracy values, shows both charts, and explains the microservices architecture with a CSS/HTML or inline SVG diagram.

assertions.description: Uses a pinned Chart.js or ECharts CDN for the charts.
Shows the user-growth values for Q1 through Q4.
Shows the model-accuracy comparison.
Shows the requested architecture components.
Uses colorblind-safe chart colors and viewport-fitting slides.
Includes keyboard navigation.

evals.name: api-metrics-review
evals.prompt: Here's our API metrics: {"endpoints": [{"path": "/users", "avg_latency_ms": 45, "p99_latency_ms": 230, "requests_per_day": 50000}, {"path": "/orders", "avg_latency_ms": 120, "p99_latency_ms": 890, "requests_per_day": 25000}, {"path": "/search", "avg_latency_ms": 200, "p99_latency_ms": 1500, "requests_per_day": 15000}], "error_rate": 0.3, "uptime": 99.95}. Create a 10-slide technical review with performance charts.
evals.expected_output: An exactly 10-slide technical API review that visualizes the supplied endpoint latency and request data, exposes the error rate and uptime, and includes a readable data table.

assertions.description: Uses the supplied endpoint data.
Shows a bar chart for average and p99 latency.
Includes multiple charts and a data table.
Shows the error-rate and uptime KPIs.
Uses the technical minimal treatment.

evals.name: microservices-teaching
evals.prompt: Make a teaching presentation about microservices architecture for a university class. Include architecture diagrams showing monolith vs microservices, a sequence flow for an API call, and code examples in Python showing a FastAPI microservice.
evals.expected_output: A readable teaching deck that contrasts monoliths and microservices, illustrates an API sequence with a CSS/HTML or inline SVG flow, and contains syntax-highlighted Python FastAPI examples.

assertions.description: Compares a monolith with microservices.
Uses a CSS or inline-SVG sequence flow.
Includes highlighted Python FastAPI code.
Uses an educational introduction, concepts, examples, and summary structure.
Keeps content in the slide viewport.

evals.name: quick-status-update
evals.prompt: Create a quick 5-slide status update with a bar chart comparing Q1 vs Q2 results: Revenue Q1=$2.1M Q2=$2.8M, Users Q1=45K Q2=62K, NPS Q1=42 Q2=51.
evals.expected_output: A concise, executive-ready five-slide status deck with a Q1 versus Q2 comparison chart and prominent Revenue, Users, and NPS KPIs.

assertions.description: Uses non-interactive defaults instead of blocking for an interview.
States the inferred audience and style choice.
Shows a Q1 versus Q2 bar chart.
Displays the supplied Revenue, Users, and NPS values.
Uses the concise executive-summary treatment.

evals.name: incremental-enhancement
evals.prompt: Add 3 slides about our new caching layer to the existing presentation at ./evals/fixtures/incremental-enhancement.html. The caching layer uses Redis with a 15-minute TTL, reduced average latency by 60%, and handles 100K requests/second. Include a before/after latency chart and a client-server diagram showing the cache.
evals.expected_output: An enhanced copy of the supplied Ocean Deep fixture that first reads its two-slide structure, preserves its visual language, and appends exactly three caching-layer slides.

assertions.description: Records the enhancement input it read.
Preserves the existing Northstar slides before adding three more.
Preserves the Ocean Deep theme, typography, and navigation.
Includes the before-and-after latency reduction.
Includes the Redis client-server diagram and TTL.
States the capacity while retaining the original deck identity.
